name: 九谷焼
area: 加賀市・能美市・小松市
desc: 石川県加賀地方で生まれた上絵付磁器。17世紀半ば、九谷の鉱山で陶石が発見され、加賀藩の職人が有田で磁器技術を習得して帰り開窯した「古九谷」に始まる。赤・緑・紫・紺青・黄の五彩を駆使した力強く豪華な絵付けが特徴で、一度廃窯の後、19世紀に再興して今日に至る。
desc_en: Kutani ware is a colorful porcelain originating from the Kaga region of Ishikawa Prefecture. Known for its bold painting using five colors (red, green, purple, dark blue, and yellow), called 'Kutani Gosai.' Founded in 1655 under the order of the Daishoji Domain, it was revived at the end of the Edo period after a period of closure.

国内外の展覧会で高い評価を受け続ける伝統と革新

desc: 佐賀県有田町を中心に生産される磁器。1616年（元和2年）、朝鮮陶工・李参平が肥前・泉山で磁器の原料となる陶石を発見したことに始まる。日本最初の磁器として知られ、江戸時代にオランダ東インド会社を通じてヨーロッパに輸出された「伊万里焼」は世界中の王侯貴族に珍重された。現在も年間600万点以上が生産され、日本最大の磁器産地。
desc_en: Arita ware is porcelain produced centered around Arita Town, Saga Prefecture. Japan's first porcelain, it began in 1616 when Korean potter Yi Sam-pyeong discovered suitable clay in Hizen-Izumiyama. Exported to Europe as 'Imari' through the Dutch East India Company, it was treasured by royalty worldwide. Today over 6 million pieces are produced annually, making it Japan's largest porcelain center.

ヨーロッパ王侯貴族を魅了した「伊万里焼」の伝統

desc_en: Kyoto ware / Kiyomizu ware is the collective term for ceramics produced in Kyoto. Nonomura Ninsei established colored porcelain techniques in the Genroku era (1688-1704), followed by Ogata Kenzan's unique designs. Deeply connected to tea ceremony culture, it is characterized by elegant and delicate beauty. Many artists continue to blend tradition and innovation in this ceramics capital.
features: 茶の湯文化と共に磨かれた繊細で上品な美しさ
野々村仁清・尾形乾山など歴代名工が生んだ豊かな意匠

desc_en: Hagi ware is pottery produced around Hagi City in Yamaguchi Prefecture. Starting in 1604 when Mori Terumoto invited Korean potters, it was beloved by tea practitioners—ranked second only to Raku ware among tea bowls. Its muted pink and cream tones and the 'Seven Transformations of Hagi' (gradual changes with use) are its greatest charms.

desc_en: Kasama ware is pottery produced in Kasama City, Ibaraki Prefecture. Dating to the mid-Edo period (1764-1772), it is the largest pottery producing area in the Kanto region. Known as 'Kasama style is individuality,' it features free expression without a fixed style. Over 100 potters work here, and the annual Himatsu Festival attracts over 200,000 visitors.

desc_en: Mashiko ware is pottery produced in Mashiko Town, Tochigi Prefecture. Started in 1853 by Otsuka Keisaburo after training in Kasama. The Living National Treasure Hamada Shoji established his base here, gaining worldwide fame through the Folk Craft Movement. Today, over 250 kilns and shops line the streets, attracting over 600,000 visitors to its bi-annual pottery markets.

desc_en: Mino ware is a collective term for ceramics produced in the Tono region of Gifu Prefecture. Production began in the late Kamakura period, producing masterpieces of tea ceramics such as Ki-Seto, Seto-guro, Shino, and Oribe. Today it holds approximately 50% of domestic tableware market share—Japan's largest ceramic production area with annual shipments exceeding 180 billion yen.

desc_en: Shigaraki ware is pottery from Shigaraki-cho, Koka City, Shiga Prefecture—one of Japan's oldest pottery-producing areas, with origins traced to 742 CE. The beauty of natural ash glaze, scorching, and ash fall created by kiln flames is its hallmark. Also world-famous for tanuki (raccoon dog) figurines. Designated a national traditional craft in 2013.

desc_en: Bizen ware is pottery produced in the Inbe district of Bizen City, Okayama Prefecture—one of Japan's Six Ancient Kilns dating to the late Heian period. Fired without glaze at 1,200-1,300°C for over two weeks, unique patterns called 'Hidasuki,' 'Botamochi,' and 'Goma' are created by fire and ash. Beloved by tea practitioners and gourmets for maturing with use.

千利休も愛した茶陶として「茶碗は一楽二萩三唐津」に並ぶ格式

desc_en: Karatsu ware is pottery produced in parts of Saga and Nagasaki Prefectures. Developed from around the 16th century using techniques brought by Korean potters, it is renowned as a top tea ceramics production area—ranked third in the saying 'First Raku, Second Hagi, Third Karatsu.' Various styles including E-Karatsu (painted), Chosen-Karatsu, and Madara-Karatsu were deeply beloved by tea masters such as Sen no Rikyu.

Characterized by hand-painted染付 (sometsuke) patterns in cobalt blue on white porcelain, it is beloved as thick, durable everyday tableware. Its simple, warm patterns are highly popular as modern tableware.

desc: 鹿児島県で生産される陶磁器。文禄・慶長の役で島津氏が連れ帰った朝鮮陶工たちによって始まり、400年以上の歴史を持つ。堅野系・龍門司系・苗代川系という異なる作風が生まれ、白薩摩（金彩色絵の豪華な磁器）と黒薩摩（鉄釉の素朴な陶器）が並立する。1867年のパリ万博でヨーロッパを席巻し、「Satsuma ware」として世界的な評価を確立した。

There are two lineages: Shiro-Satsuma (white porcelain with gold painting and colored decoration) and Kuro-Satsuma (iron-rich black and amber earthenware). White Satsuma was exported to Europe and America in the Meiji era, gaining worldwide recognition as 'Satsuma ware.'

There are two types: 'Arayachi' (unglazed) and 'Joyachi' (glazed). Famous for Shisa lion-dogs and Dachijin (flat flasks), the 'Yachimun Street' in Naha is a tourist spot for craft enthusiasts.

desc: 大分県日田市源栄町皿山地区で生産される陶器。1705年頃、小石原焼の陶工・柳瀬三右衛門を招いて開窯したとされる。飛び鉋（とびかんな）・刷毛目・打ち刷毛目など独特の装飾技法と、藁灰釉の素朴な美しさが世界的に評価されている。民藝運動の柳宗悦・バーナード・リーチも絶賛した日本民窯の代表例。10軒の窯元のみが生産を担い、分業せず一家で全工程を行う伝統を守っている。
desc_en: Onta ware is pottery produced in Sarayama district, Hita City, Oita Prefecture. Established around 1705 when potter Yanase Mitsaemon from Koishiwara ware was invited to open a kiln. Its unique decorative techniques (tobikanna, hakeme, etc.) and rustic beauty with straw ash glaze are internationally recognized. Praised by Yanagi Soetsu and Bernard Leach of the Folk Craft Movement, only 10 kilns produce it, with each family handling the entire process without division of labor.

desc: 福島県双葉郡浪江町大堀地区が発祥の陶器。1690年頃、相馬藩の奨励によって始まったとされる。「二重焼」と呼ばれる二重構造の器・駿馬（走り駒）の絵付け・「青ひび」と呼ばれるひび割れ模様（貫入）が三大特徴。2011年の東日本大震災・原発事故による避難で産地が一時消滅の危機に瀕したが、現在は避難先などで復興活動が続けられている。
desc_en: Ohori Soma ware originated in Ohori district, Namie Town, Futaba-gun, Fukushima Prefecture. Said to have started around 1690 with encouragement from the Soma domain. Its three defining features are: 'Niijuyaki' (double-walled structure), horse paintings (hashiri-koma), and 'Ao-hibi' (blue crackle glaze). After the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and nuclear accident forced evacuation, the production area faced near-extinction, but revival efforts continue at relocation sites.

desc: 愛知県瀬戸市で生産される陶磁器。平安末期から続く日本六古窯の一つで、江戸時代に磁器の技術を取り入れ「染付磁器」の生産を始めた。「瀬戸物」という言葉が陶磁器全般の代名詞となるほど普及した歴史を持つ。現在も日本有数の陶磁器産地として、窯業従事者数・出荷額ともに全国上位を誇る。
desc_en: Seto ware is ceramics produced in Seto City, Aichi Prefecture—one of Japan's Six Ancient Kilns dating to the late Heian period. By incorporating porcelain techniques in the Edo period and producing染付磁器 (sometsuke porcelain), it became so widespread that 'setomono' became a generic word for ceramics. It remains one of Japan's leading ceramic production areas.

desc_en: Shodai ware is pottery produced mainly in Arao City and Tamana City, Kumamoto Prefecture. Said to have started around 1632 with encouragement from the Higo Hosokawa clan. Characterized by flowing 'nagashikake' patterns of straw ash glaze and rustic clay textures, its style aligned with the folk craft spirit of 'beauty in use' has been beloved by tea practitioners and mingei enthusiasts.
features: 流れるような藁灰釉の景色が醸す「用の美」
細川家御用窯から続く約400年の歴史
民藝運動にも評価された素朴で力強い土の表情

Founded after the Korean invasions of 1598 by Korean potters, it flourished during the Edo period as affordable everyday tableware. Known for simple, timeless designs and accessible pricing, it has grown into a popular brand among younger generations today.

desc_en: Mikawachi ware is a fine white porcelain produced in the Mikawachi area of Sasebo City, Nagasaki Prefecture. Descended from Korean potters brought over in 1598, it served as the official kiln of the Hirado Domain in the Edo period. It is best known for its "Karako-e" motif depicting Chinese-style children at play, combined with luminous white porcelain.

desc: 福岡県東峰村で生産される陶器。17世紀前期（江戸時代前期）に黒田藩主が筑前最初の窯を開き、当初は「中野焼」と呼ばれ磁器を焼いていたが、18世紀初めから陶器の生産に移行し「小石原焼」の名が定着した。飛び鉋・刷毛目・流し掛けなどの技法による幾何学的な文様が特徴で、民藝の「用の美」を体現した実用的な器として高く評価される。
desc_en: Koishiwara ware is produced in Toho Village, Fukuoka Prefecture. Founded in 1682 when the third lord of the Fukuoka domain brought potters from Imari, it is characterized by geometric patterns created through techniques such as "tobikanna" (skipping chisel), brush strokes, and poured glazes. It is highly regarded as functional pottery embodying the folk craft philosophy of "beauty in use."

desc_en: Takatori ware is a tea ceramics produced in Fukuoka Prefecture. Established in 1606 when Kuroda Nagamasa invited Korean potter Hachiyama (Hachizo), it is known as one of the "Enshu Seven Kilns" of tea ceremony ceramics. Characterized by thin, lightweight vessels with a refined wabi aesthetic, featuring complex glaze effects from layered white, yellow, black, and iron glazes.

desc_en: Banko ware is produced primarily in Yokkaichi City, Mie Prefecture. Founded around 1736 by Numami Rozan, the name "Banko" means "eternal and unchanging." Today it is nationally known for everyday items such as teapots and clay pots, with Banko teapots accounting for approximately 80% of Japan's teapot production.

desc: 福井県越前町で生産される陶器で、日本六古窯の一つ。平安時代末期に始まり、約900年の歴史を持つ。釉薬を使わず薪窯で焼成する「無釉焼締め」が基本で、灰や炎の作用によって生まれる自然釉（ビードロ釉）と焦げが器に独特の表情を与える。壺・甕・擂鉢などの実用的な器が中心。
desc_en: Echizen ware is produced in Echizen Town, Fukui Prefecture, and is one of Japan's Six Ancient Kilns. Beginning in the late Heian period, it has approximately 900 years of history. The basic technique is "unglazed stoneware" fired in wood kilns, where natural ash glazes and scorching create unique surfaces on the vessels. It centers on practical forms such as jars, crocks, and mortars.

Characterized by the "hand-building" technique without a wheel, it is fired at low temperatures, resulting in lightweight vessels that embody the wabi aesthetic cherished by tea practitioners. The tradition has been preserved through generations of the Raku family.

name: 大谷焼
desc: 徳島県鳴門市で生産される陶器。安永9年（1780年）に藩窯として磁器の生産を試みたが短期間で閉窯し、天明4年（1784年）に信楽焼の職人を招いた民窯が大谷村に設立されたのが実質的な始まり。一人が横になってろくろを踏み、もう一人が成形する「寝ろくろ」という独特の技法で大型の甕・壺を作り、藍染め産業を支えた。
desc_en: Otani ware is produced in Naruto City, Tokushima Prefecture. Beginning around 1780, it is characterized by a unique technique called "nerokkuro" (lying-down wheel) used to make large vessels. Two potters work together, with one lying down to turn the wheel while the other shapes the clay, producing large urns and jars used in indigo dyeing. Today it is preserved as a traditional industry of Tokushima.
features: 一人が横になってろくろを踏む「寝ろくろ」という世界でも珍しい技法
藍染め産業を支えた大型甕・壺の生産から始まった歴史
徳島・阿波の伝統を受け継ぐ四国最大の陶器産地

name: 赤津焼
desc: 愛知県瀬戸市赤津地区で生産される陶器で、日本六古窯「瀬戸焼」の中核産地の一つ。奈良時代（700年頃）に焼かれた須恵器に始まり、桃山〜江戸初期に志野・織部・黄瀬戸・御深井などの釉薬技法が確立されて尾張徳川家の御用窯として栄えた。これら「古瀬戸」の伝統釉薬技術が現在まで受け継がれている。
desc_en: Akatsu ware is produced in the Akatsu district of Seto City, Aichi Prefecture, and is one of the core areas of "Seto ware" within Japan's Six Ancient Kilns. With a history dating to the Kamakura period, it is known as a producer that preserves traditional glazes called "Ko-Seto" (ash glaze, yellow Seto, Seto black, Shino, and Oribe). Its diverse glazing techniques represent an important legacy in the history of Japanese ceramics.
features: 鎌倉時代から続く「古瀬戸」の伝統釉薬を現代に伝える
灰釉・黄瀬戸・瀬戸黒・志野・織部など多彩な釉薬の宝庫
日本六古窯・瀬戸焼の歴史を最も色濃く残す産地

name: 大樋焼
desc: 石川県金沢市で生産される陶器で、1666年（寛文6年）に加賀藩主前田綱紀が茶の湯を奨励した際、裏千家四世仙叟宗室とともに京都から招かれた陶工・長左衛門（後の大樋長左衛門）が始めた。「飴釉（あめぐすり）」と呼ばれる独特の黄褐色の釉薬と、手びねりによる温かみある土物の茶道具が特徴。裏千家の御好み焼として現在も大樋家十一代が伝統を受け継ぎ、加賀百万石の茶道文化を体現する茶陶として400年近く金沢で作り続けられている。
desc_en: Ohi Ware is a ceramic produced in Kanazawa City, Ishikawa Prefecture, begun in 1666 by a potter named Chozaemon (later Ohi Chozaemon) who was invited from Kyoto along with Ura Senke's 4th master, Senso Soshitsu, when the Kaga domain lord encouraged the tea ceremony. Characterized by a distinctive amber-brown glaze called 'ame-gusuri' and warm, hand-formed tea utensils. Still produced by the 11th generation of the Ohi family as the preferred ware of Ura Senke, embodying Kaga's tea culture for nearly 400 years.
features: 裏千家御好み焼として400年近く継承される加賀の代表的茶陶
「飴釉」による独特の黄褐色と手びねりの温かみある造形
大樋家が一子相伝で守り続ける金沢茶道文化の象徴

name: 石見焼
desc: 島根県江津市を中心に生産される陶器。江戸時代中期に地元職人が山口県の陶工から製陶法を習ったことに始まり、その後備前から大型甕の技術も取り入れ産地として発展した。塩蔵・味噌・醤油用の大型甕「石見甕」は全国に流通した。現在も薪窯で焼き締める素朴な陶器や日常食器が作られ、土の風合いと実用美が親しまれている。
desc_en: Iwami Ware is a ceramic produced mainly in Goto City, Shimane Prefecture, developing from the late Edo to Meiji period as a producer of large jars, pots, and bowls. Using high-quality clay from the Iwami region and wood-fired kiln techniques, it is known for its rustic yet powerful character. Large storage jars called 'Iwami-gama' were distributed nationwide for salt, miso, and soy sauce preservation. Today it also produces everyday tableware and plant pots, beloved for its natural clay texture and functional beauty.
features: 全国に流通した「石見甕」に代表される素朴で力強い大型陶器
石見地方の良質な陶土と薪窯焼き締めによる優れた保存性能
江戸後期から続く民衆の生活を支えた実用陶器の産地

name: 肥前吉田焼
desc: 佐賀県嬉野市吉田地区で生産される磁器で、有田焼・伊万里焼と同じ肥前磁器の産地として知られる。薄手で軽く丈夫な白磁・染付の日常食器の生産が盛んで、「薄くて軽い吉田焼」として家庭用食器市場で高いシェアを誇る。肥前の磁器産地として確立した技術力をもとに、現代では国内外への量産食器とともに作家的な作品も生まれており、有田・波佐見と並ぶ肥前の磁器文化を支える重要産地の一つ。
desc_en: Hizen Yoshida Ware is a porcelain produced in the Yoshida district of Ureshino City, Saga Prefecture, known as a Hizen porcelain production area alongside Arita and Imari ware. Famous for thin, light, and durable white porcelain and blue-and-white everyday tableware, it holds a high share of the household tableware market as 'thin and light Yoshida ware.' Based on established porcelain craftsmanship, today it produces both mass-market tableware for domestic and overseas markets and individual artistic works, making it a key production area supporting Hizen's porcelain culture.
features: 薄くて軽い実用的な白磁・染付食器で家庭用市場を支える産地
有田・波佐見と並ぶ肥前磁器文化の一翼を担う歴史ある産地
日常食器から現代作家作品まで幅広く展開する多様な表現

name: 三州鬼瓦工芸品
desc: 愛知県高浜市を中心に生産される鬼瓦・装飾瓦の工芸品。18世紀初頭から生産が活発化し、300年以上の伝統を持つ。「鬼師」と呼ばれる職人が手彫りで仕上げる魔除けの鬼瓦のほか、家紋入りや室内用のインテリア・エクステリア商品まで多岐にわたる。日本の屋根瓦の約7割を占める三州瓦産地の高度な彫塑技術の結晶として今も継承される。
desc_en: Sanshu Onigawara are ornamental demon-face roof tiles and decorative tiles produced mainly in Takahama City, Aichi Prefecture. As a Sanshu roof tile production area dating to the Muromachi period, the demon-face tiles ('onigawara') used to ward off evil from rooftops are individually crafted sculptures carved by hand. Sanshu tiles made from local clay—with excellent compressive strength and low water absorption—account for approximately 70% of Japan's roof tiles. The ornamental demon tiles represent the pinnacle of this region's sculptural craftsmanship.
features: 職人「鬼師」の手彫りによる魔除けの伝統彫刻工芸品
日本の屋根瓦の約7割を占める三州瓦産地の最高技術の結晶

name: 今戸焼
desc: 東京都台東区今戸（浅草付近）を発祥とする素朴な土焼きの工芸品。江戸時代から庶民の生活雑器・火鉢・植木鉢・土人形を生産してきた江戸の焼き物文化を代表する産地。現在は白い「招き猫」の発祥地として広く知られており、素朴で温かみある土人形・置物が特徴。明治以降の近代化で産地は大幅に縮小したものの、今も職人が江戸庶民の焼き物文化を伝える伝統を守り続けている。
desc_en: Imado Ware originates from the Imado area (near Asakusa) in Taito Ward, Tokyo, representing a rustic earthenware craft tradition. Since the Edo period, it has been a production area for everyday utensils, braziers, plant pots, and clay figurines for the common people. Today it is widely known as the birthplace of the white 'manekineko' (beckoning cat), characterized by rustic yet warm clay figurines and ornaments. Though the production area significantly declined after the Meiji modernization, craftsmen continue to preserve this Edo-era folk pottery tradition.
features: 江戸庶民の生活文化から生まれた素朴な土人形・招き猫の発祥地
火鉢・植木鉢など日常雑器から縁起物まで幅広い江戸の焼き物
